summary: Pin `--dry-run` into the examples of the four mutating File Station commands and mark all six as `mcp:read-only: false`.
reason: Two defects meet on the same commands. First, the live dogfood harness executes a command's `example:` string verbatim against the real target rather than dry-running it, so the corrected examples for `files mkdir`, `rename`, `copy-start` and `delete-start` actually created, renamed and copied entries on a live DS415+, and consecutive runs were not idempotent: the second run failed because the first had already renamed the source. The harness also requires an Examples section in `--help`, so dropping the example is not an option; carrying `--dry-run` inside it is, and it doubles as the right thing to show a human reading `--help` for a destructive command. Second, the generator infers `mcp:read-only` from the HTTP method, and DSM tunnels every mutation through GET, so all six mutating commands shipped annotated as read-only - an MCP client that auto-approves read-only tools would have called `files delete-start` without asking.
coverage_impact: The happy-path and JSON-fidelity probes for the four commands now exercise request construction rather than a live mutation. Transport, auth and response handling for these endpoints are covered only by their non-mutating siblings.
validated_outcome: `dogfood --live --level full` reports 192 passed, 0 failed, `Verdict: PASS (with skips)`, and writes `status: pass`; a live run leaves no new entries on the NAS.
